question_text: In hexagonal/clean architecture, what rule governs dependency direction across domain, application, and infrastructure layers?

options.text: The Domain layer must depend on Infrastructure data repositories via concrete classes
Dependencies must point strictly inwards towards the Domain; outer layers depend on abstractions defined by inner layers
Application layer must not have access to domain entities
Infrastructure layer controls all business workflow transitions

answer_explanation: The Dependency Inversion Principle mandates that core business logic (Domain) remains free of external framework or persistence dependencies, defining interfaces that outer adapters implement.
reference_solution: Correct Choice: B. Rationale: The Dependency Inversion Principle mandates that core business logic (Domain) remains free of external framework or persistence dependencies, defining interfaces that outer adapters implement.

criteria.name: Correctness
criteria.description: Selects the exact correct technical option.
